questions.question: Which of the following describes a key function of lysosomal enzymes?

options.text: Breaking down proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates
Creating new proteins for the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breaking down proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles containing a variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (acid hydrolases) that are capable of digesting all types of biological polymers.
 
• The primary function of these enzymes is **intracellular digestion**, where they break down macromolecules such as **proteins**, **lipids**, **polysaccharides**, and **nucleic acids** into their basic building blocks.
 
• These enzymes function most efficiently in an **acidic environment**, typically maintaining a **pH of about 4.5 to 5.0** within the lysosomal lumen, which is regulated by **proton pumps** in the membrane.
 
• Lysosomes are often referred to as the **suicide bags** of the cell because if the cell is damaged beyond repair, the lysosomes can burst and release enzymes to digest the entire cell, a process known as **autolysis**.
 
• Beyond digestion of external materials, they are essential for **autophagy**, which involves the degradation of the cell's own obsolete or damaged **organelles** to recycle nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Storing genetic material**:

 
 
• This is the function of the **Nucleus**, which contains the cell's **DNA** organized into **chromosomes**.
 
 
 
• **Transporting molecules across the membrane**:
 
 
• This role is performed by the **Plasma Membrane** (cell membrane) through mechanisms like **active transport**, **facilitated diffusion**, and **ion channels**.
 
 
 
• **Creating new proteins for the cell**:
 
 
• This is the primary function of **Ribosomes**, which can be found in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery**:
 
 
• Lysosomes were discovered by the Belgian cytologist **Christian de Duve** in **1955**, for which he later received a **Nobel Prize**.

questions.question: Metals like iron and zinc, which are in the middle of the activity series, are generally summarized (concluded) as follows:

options.text: A heating process involving no reducing agent of any kind.
Reduction of their oxides with carbon or carbon monoxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of their oxides with carbon or carbon monoxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals placed in the **middle of the reactivity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, and **Copper (Cu)**, are considered moderately reactive and are often found as **sulfide** or **carbonate** ores.
 
• Since extracting a metal from its **oxide** is chemically more efficient, these ores are first converted into oxides through **Roasting** (heating sulfide ores in excess air) or **Calcination** (heating carbonate ores in limited air).
 
• The **metal oxides** are then **reduced** to their respective metallic states using a suitable **reducing agent** like **carbon (coke)** or **carbon monoxide**.
 
• This chemical process, known as **Smelting**, involves the carbon reacting with the oxygen in the metal oxide to form carbon dioxide or monoxide, leaving behind the metal: **ZnO + C → Zn + CO**.
 
• For **Iron**, the reduction occurs in a **blast furnace** where **carbon monoxide (CO)** acts as the primary reducing agent to convert **Haematite (Fe₂O₃)** into molten iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis of molten salts**

 
 
• This method is utilized for **highly reactive metals** (e.g., **Sodium**, **Aluminium**, **Calcium**) located at the top of the activity series.
 
• These metals have a very high **affinity for oxygen**, making it impossible to reduce them using carbon.
 
 
 
• **Heating without a reducing agent (Self-reduction)**
 
 
• Metals at the **bottom of the activity series** (e.g., **Mercury**, **Silver**) are so unreactive that their oxides can be reduced to metal by **heat alone**.
 
• For example, **Cinnabar (HgS)** is converted to **Mercuric Oxide (HgO)** and then reduced to **Mercury (Hg)** simply by continued heating.
 
 
 
• **Displacement from aqueous solution**
 
 
• Used for extracting less reactive metals by treating their **salt solutions** with a **more reactive metal** (e.g., using **Iron** to displace **Copper** from **Copper Sulfate**).

questions.question: A bus moves from one end A to the other end B of a straight 1000 m road in 100 s and then turns around and moves 500 m back to point C in another 100 s. What will be the average velocity (in m/s) and the type of motion of the bus in going from point A to point C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5 m/s and Non-Uniform Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the shortest straight-line distance between the **initial position** (Point A) and the **final position** (Point C). The bus travels 1000 m from A to B and then returns 500 m towards A to reach C. Therefore, the net displacement is 1000 − 500 = **500 meters**.
 
• The **total time taken** for the entire journey from A to C is the sum of the time taken from A to B and from B to C. This equals 100 s + 100 s = **200 seconds**.
 
• **Average Velocity** is calculated by dividing the **total displacement** by the **total time taken**. Using the values derived, Average Velocity = 500 / 200 = **2.5 m/s**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion** occurs when an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time or when its **direction of motion** changes. In this scenario, the bus moves at 10 m/s (1000/100) initially and then at 5 m/s (500/100) in the opposite direction. Since the **velocity** (magnitude and direction) is not constant, the motion is classified as **Non-Uniform**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion**:

 
 
• An object is said to be in **uniform motion** if it travels in a straight line and covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**.
 
• The **acceleration** in uniform motion is always **zero** because the velocity remains constant throughout the duration of the movement.
 
 
 
• **Average Speed**:
 
 
• Unlike velocity, **average speed** depends on the **total distance** traveled rather than displacement.
 
• For this journey, the total distance is 1000 + 500 = 1500 m. The average speed would be 1500 / 200 = **7.5 m/s**.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** requiring both magnitude and direction, whereas **speed** is a **scalar quantity**.

questions.question:
Examine the two statements given below and select the correct option.

Statement A: Nervous tissue is responsible for the rapid transmission of electrical impulses within the body.

Statement B: Nervous tissue primarily provides structural and mechanical support to organs.

options.text: A is not correct, but B is correct.
Two statements, A and B, are not correct.
A is correct, but B is not correct.
Two statements, A and B, are correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is correct, but B is not correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nervous tissue** is highly specialized to receive **stimuli** and transmit **electrical impulses** (action potentials) throughout the body to coordinate various functions. Hence, statement A is correct.
 
• The **neurons**, which are the functional units of the nervous system, possess the property of **excitability** and **conductivity**, allowing for the rapid relay of information across **synapses**. Hence, statement A is correct.
 
• **Connective tissue**, rather than nervous tissue, is the primary tissue responsible for providing **structural and mechanical support**, protection, and binding of different organs. Hence, statement B is incorrect.
 
• While **nervous tissue** facilitates communication and control, it lacks the dense **extracellular matrix** (like collagen fibers found in connective tissue) required to serve as a structural framework. Hence, statement B is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of Nervous Tissue**:

 
 
• **Neurons**: Specialized cells consisting of a **cell body (cyton)**, **dendrites** (receive signals), and a long **axon** (transmits signals).
 
• **Neuroglia**: Also called **glial cells**, these provide metabolic support, insulation (via **myelin sheaths**), and protection to neurons but do not conduct impulses.
 
 
 
• **Other Primary Tissue Types**:
 
 
• **Epithelial Tissue**: Functions in protection, secretion, and absorption across **membranes** and **glandular structures**.
 
• **Muscular Tissue**: Composed of elongated cells that contract to produce **locomotion** and movement within internal organs.
 
• **Connective Tissue**: Includes specialized forms like **bone**, **cartilage**, and **adipose tissue**, which provide the actual mechanical strength and support to the human anatomy.

questions.question: In September 2025, what significant legal position did the Supreme Court of India reiterate under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?

options.text: The accused may apply for anticipatory bail under all circumstances.
The provision for anticipatory bail has been removed from the Indian Penal Code.
If a crime under the law is revealed upon a prima facie examination of the FIR, the granting of anticipatory bail is strictly prohibited.
Only the High Court can grant anticipatory bail.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**If a crime under the law is revealed upon a prima facie examination of the FIR, the granting of anticipatory bail is strictly prohibited.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** reiterated the absolute bar on granting **anticipatory bail** under **Section 18** of the **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989**, provided the **First Information Report (FIR)** discloses a **prima facie** case.
 
• Under this legal framework, **Section 438** of the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**, or the corresponding **Section 482** of the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, does not apply to offenses registered under the **SC/ST Act**.
 
• The **prima facie** standard implies that the court must only examine if the essential ingredients of the offense are mentioned in the complaint without a deep merit-based mini-trial at the bail stage.
 
• The judicial intent behind this restriction is to protect **marginalized communities** from **intimidation** and ensure that the accused do not evade the immediate legal process in serious cases of **social discrimination** and **violence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989**:

 
 
• **Section 18A**: This was inserted through a **2018 Amendment** to nullify a previous judgment that had introduced requirements for **preliminary inquiries** and prior approvals for arrest.
 
• **Judicial Precedents**: In the landmark **Prathvi Raj Chauhan vs. Union of India (2020)** case, the **Supreme Court** upheld the constitutional validity of **Section 18A**, affirming that **anticipatory bail** can only be granted in exceptional cases where no **prima facie case** is established.
 
• **Scope of Atrocities**: The Act defines specific crimes against **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes**, including **social boycott**, **forced labor**, and **assault** on women, providing for **Special Courts** to ensure speedy justice.

questions.question: In which Indian state do the Western Ghats reach their maximum elevation, home to Anaimudi—the highest peak in this mountain range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Ghats**, also known as the **Sahyadri** mountains, constitute a **1,600-kilometer** long range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula, passing through six states.
 
• The state of **Kerala** hosts the highest elevation of the entire range at **Anaimudi** peak, which stands at an altitude of **2,695 meters** (**8,842 feet**) above mean sea level.
 
• Located in the **Idukki district**, **Anaimudi** is famously known as the **Everest of South India** because it is the highest point in India south of the **Himalayas**.
 
• The peak is situated at the strategic junction of three mountain sub-ranges: the **Annamalai Hills** to the north, the **Palani Hills** to the northeast, and the **Cardamom Hills** to the south.
 
• Geographically, this region is part of the **Eravikulam National Park**, which serves as a critical conservation zone for the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered mountain ungulate endemic to these hills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Peaks in Other States**:

 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**: The highest peak is **Doddabetta** in the **Nilgiri Hills**, reaching an elevation of **2,637 meters**, making it the second-highest peak in the Western Ghats.
 
• **Karnataka**: The highest point is **Mullayanagiri** in the **Chikkamagaluru** district, standing at approximately **1,930 meters** within the **Chandra Dhrona Hill Range**.
 
• **Maharashtra**: The highest elevation is the **Kalsubai Shikhar**, which reaches **1,646 meters** and is a prominent trekking destination in the **Sahyadri** range.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**:
 
 
• The Western Ghats are a recognized **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and represent one of the world's eight **biodiversity hotspots**.
 
• The range influences the **Indian Monsoon** by acting as an **orographic barrier**, forcing moisture-laden winds from the **Arabian Sea** to rise and release heavy rainfall on the windward side.

questions.question: In which year did India sign the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement and become a founding member of WTO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Trade Organization (WTO)** officially commenced its operations on **January 1, 1995**, following the conclusion of the **Uruguay Round** of negotiations that lasted from **1986** to **1994**.
 
• **India** is a **founding member** of the **WTO**, having been one of the **123 nations** that signed the **Marrakesh Agreement** on **April 15, 1994**, in **Morocco**.
 
• Before the **WTO** was established, India was an original signatory to the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** since **1947**, which served as the predecessor to the **WTO**.
 
• The transition to the **WTO** in **1995** expanded the scope of international trade rules to include **Trade in Services (GATS)** and **Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)**, alongside trade in goods.
 
• By becoming a founding member in **1995**, India gained a platform to negotiate **multilateral trade agreements** and access the **Dispute Settlement Body** to resolve international trade conflicts.

• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:

 
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, and functions as the primary body for supervising and liberalizing **international trade**.
 
• It operates on principles such as **Most Favored Nation (MFN)** status and **National Treatment** to ensure non-discriminatory trade between member countries.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 1991**:
 
 
• While India joined the **WTO** in **1995**, the groundwork was laid in **1991** when the Indian government introduced **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** reforms under the **New Economic Policy**.
 
 
 
• **Uruguay Round**:
 
 
• This was the **8th round** of multilateral trade negotiations conducted within the framework of **GATT**, leading to the largest reform of the world's trading system since **1947**.

questions.question: "To provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years" was added to the Indian Constitution as the 11th Fundamental Duty through which of the following amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** were not part of the original **Constitution of India**; they were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, introduced **Part IV-A** and **Article 51A**, which originally listed **10 Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, expanded this list by adding the **11th Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)**.
 
• This duty mandates that a parent or guardian must provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of **6 and 14 years**.
 
• The amendment serves as a bridge between the **Fundamental Rights** of the child and the moral obligations of the parents, ensuring the success of the **Right to Education**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**:

 
 
• Often called the **Mini-Constitution**, it added the words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** to the **Preamble** and established the primary framework for **Fundamental Duties**.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**:
 
 
• This amendment was passed to nullify several provisions of the **42nd Amendment** and is notable for removing the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights**, making it a legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988**:
 
 
• This act amended **Article 326** to lower the **voting age** for elections to the **Lok Sabha** and the **Legislative Assemblies** from **21 years to 18 years**.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**:
 
 
• Concurrently introduced by the **86th Amendment**, it made **Free and Compulsory Education** a **Fundamental Right** for all children in the **6 to 14 age group**.

questions.question: The National Sports Governance Bill, 2025, was introduced to achieve which of the following objective?

options.text: To increase budget allocation for Olympic sports
To launch a national-level talent hunt program
To establish rules for recognizing and regulating sports bodies
To improve physical and sports education in schools

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To establish rules for recognizing and regulating sports bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Sports Governance Bill, 2025**, is designed to provide a statutory framework for the **governance** and **regulation** of sports in India, effectively codifying the **National Sports Development Code of India** into law.
 
• Its primary objective is to establish a **Sports Regulatory Board of India**, which will be responsible for **granting recognition** to **National Sports Federations (NSFs)** and the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** based on strict compliance with governance standards.
 
• The bill mandates **transparency** and **accountability** by requiring sports bodies to maintain **audited financial statements** and placing them under the purview of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act**.
 
• It aims to eliminate **administrative monopolies** by enforcing **age and tenure restrictions** for office-bearers, ensuring that no individual holds a leadership position indefinitely.
 
• The legislation introduces a structured process for the **suspension** or **withdrawal of recognition** if a sports body fails to meet the criteria for **ethical management** and **fair elections**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sports Regulatory Board**: Acts as the primary oversight body to monitor **NSF elections** and **financial disclosures**.
 
• **Appellate Sports Tribunal**: A dedicated legal body established under the bill to settle **sports-related disputes** and **grievances**, reducing reliance on civil courts.
 
• **Athletes Commission**: Every recognized federation must establish a commission to ensure **athlete representation** in the decision-making process.
 
• **Gender Equality**: The bill promotes inclusivity by mandating a minimum **30 percent representation** for women in the **Executive Committees** of sports bodies.
 
• **Olympic Charter Compliance**: The framework ensures that Indian domestic law remains aligned with the principles of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** and the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**.

questions.question: Through which Constitutional Amendment was the term 'Armed Rebellion' introduced under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution for the declaration of a National Emergency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978** was enacted by the **Janata Government** to undo several changes made by the **42nd Amendment** and to provide safeguards against future misuse of emergency powers.
 
• Before this amendment, **Article 352** allowed the declaration of a **National Emergency** on the grounds of **war**, **external aggression**, or **internal disturbance**.
 
• The term **'internal disturbance'** was considered too vague and was replaced by **'armed rebellion'** to ensure that a National Emergency could only be proclaimed in the event of a grave security threat involving physical violence.
 
• This amendment also introduced the requirement that the **President** can only issue a proclamation of emergency after receiving a **written recommendation** from the **Union Cabinet**.
 
• Furthermore, it provided that the proclamation must be approved by both **Houses of Parliament** within **one month** by a **special majority**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**:

 
 
• Often called the **Mini-Constitution**, it added the words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** to the **Preamble**.
 
• It introduced **Fundamental Duties** (Part IV-A) and restricted the power of the **Judiciary** regarding constitutional validity.
 
 
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988**:
 
 
• This act amended **Article 326** of the Constitution.
 
• It reduced the **voting age** for elections to the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies** from **21 years to 18 years**.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**:
 
 
• Inserted **Article 21A**, making **Right to Education** a **Fundamental Right** for children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• It also added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents and guardians.
